facts.value: Cognitive psychology focuses on brain science and how our mental processes such as thinking, remembering, and learning function. A cognitive psychologist may work in a private or government research facility, university, or clinical setting to conduct research on how the brain processes, stores, and retrieves information.

Developmental psychology focuses on the study of how we as humans grow, change, and adapt at different life stages. This includes how we change physically, cognitively, intellectually, and emotionally.

Social psychology focuses on how we as individuals influence and relate to each other and our social environments. Why do we think and behave the way we do in a group setting? How do other people influence our decisions? How can we deal with social challenges such as discrimination, bullying, or criminal behavior?

Personality psychology studies the nature of personality, its traits, structure, and development, as well as dysfunctional forms such as personality disorders. Personality psychologists look at how our personalities are unique to us as individuals and how we share similarities that can help us better understand overall human behavior.

Industrial-organizational (I-O) psychology focuses on human behavior in the workplace and within corporate organizations with the aim of resolving problems at work. I/O psychologists study areas of employment such as recruitment, training, motivation, performance assessment, and work-life balance.
Forensic psychology applies psychology principles to criminal investigations and the law.
School psychology aims to help students cope with learning and behavioral issues at school or university.
Health psychology focuses on the psychological aspects of coping with physical illness.

Psychology is a science that explores mental states, cognitive processes, and behaviors in both humans and animals. The discipline is divided between a science of the mind, brain, and social behavior and a professional practice; some psychologists integrate the two.
Psychology is a scientific discipline that studies mental states and processes and behavior in humans and other animals.
Psychologists study mental and biological processes and behavior in humans and other animals using diverse research methods.
Psychologists use experiments by manipulating variables and observing outcomes in controlled environments, involving experimental and control groups.
In psychology, thoughts, feelings, and behaviors are interconnected but distinct elements.
Psychologists employ various methods such as assessments and psychotherapy techniques to support individuals facing mental health challenges.
Major branches of psychology include Biological Psychology, Clinical Psychology, Cognitive Psychology, Developmental Psychology, and Social Psychology.
